closing_note:
Completed Tier 1 tpcgen-cli 4.0.0 parity spike on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 (10 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, Python 3.11.17, PyArrow 24.0.0, DuckDB 2.0.0, DataFusion 55.0.0).

1. TPC-H (SF 0.01, 0.1, 1.0) — FULL PASS (GO):
- Delimited: 8/8 tables 100% SHA-256 byte-identical vs bundled dbgen at --num-threads 1 and default threads once trailing '|' is stripped from tpcgen-cli output (thread_invariant=True).
- Parquet: bidirectional DuckDB EXCEPT ALL = 0 rows on 8/8 tables at all 3 scales.
- SF 1.0 speed & RSS: legacy dbgen 12.69s + Parquet convert 3.38s = 16.07s total vs tpcgen-cli tbl 1.34s (9.4x faster, 931.6 MiB RSS; 1t: 3.39s, 528.6 MiB) and direct parquet 2.52s (6.4x faster, 616.2 MiB).

2. TPC-DS (SF 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, --compat c) — SF 1.0 FULL PASS, SF < 1.0 BLOCKED:
- SF 1.0: 24/24 tables 100% SHA-256 byte-identical vs bundled dsdgen at --num-threads 1 and default threads (thread_invariant=True, exact UTF-8 and NULL/empty-string parity); bidirectional DuckDB EXCEPT ALL = 0 rows on 24/24 Parquet tables.
- SF 1.0 speed & RSS: legacy dsdgen 58.34s + Parquet convert 5.48s = 63.82s total vs tpcgen-cli dat 0.91s (64.2x faster, 156.5 MiB RSS; 1t: 5.13s, 31.3 MiB) and direct parquet 1.05s (60.8x faster, 586.0 MiB).
- SF 0.01 & 0.1 (GAP -> block native for tpcds SF < 1.0): tpcgen-cli uses a different fractional scaling curve than BenchBox's patched dsdgen (17/24 tables mismatch at SF 0.01, 15/24 at SF 0.1; e.g., customer_demographics=1,920,800, reason=75, item=2,000, store_sales=120,527 vs 28,810). Only the 7 fixed-size tables (catalog_page, date_dim, household_demographics, income_band, ship_mode, warehouse, time_dim) match byte-for-byte. Disposition: restrict tpcgen-cli TPC-DS adapter to SF >= 1.0 (integer scales); keep dsdgen for fractional TPC-DS sub-scales (and file upstream issue).

3. Framing, Streaming, Parts & Schema Findings (Adapter Shims):
- Framing bug caught: normalize_tbl_trailing_delimiters() in benchbox/core/tpch/generator.py checks only the last 3 bytes, which corrupts tables whose final column can be empty (stripped 50,400 separators on TPC-DS time_dim.dat). Disposition: Phase 1 adapter must strip trailing '|' unconditionally from tpcgen-cli output only.
- --stdout streaming: verified SHA-256 identical to file output (tpch:lineitem and tpcds:store_sales), enabling single-pass strip + zstd compression without disk rewrite.
- --parts layout: tpcgen-cli writes nested <table>/<table>.<part>.<ext>; adapter must map/stream to BenchBox's flat <table>.<ext>.<part>.<comp> naming.
- Exclude dbgen_version from TPC-DS table list (tpcgen-cli defaults to 25 tables including dbgen_version).
- Parquet logical types: tpcgen-cli emits string_view (vs BenchBox string) and int32 (vs int64 for INTEGER) on both TPC-H & TPC-DS, plus decimal128(7,2) (vs decimal128(15,2)) on TPC-DS.
- Parquet physical layout & scan timing (CONFIRMS OPT-IN POLICY): legacy converter wrote 1 RG/table (TPCH 8 RGs / 303.4 MiB; TPCDS 24 RGs / 383.1 MiB) vs tpcgen-cli 7MiB RGs (TPCH 94 RGs / 345.0 MiB; TPCDS 72 RGs / 398.8 MiB). On identical data (identical result_digest on both engines), Parquet scan timings shifted 4.6x–9.4x (DuckDB Q1 141.4ms->25.5ms, Q6 71.1ms->15.4ms; DataFusion Q1 264.5ms->40.0ms, Q6 171.6ms->18.2ms; DuckDB ss_agg 46.4ms->7.9ms). Direct Parquet MUST stay opt-in and tracked in data_generation_hash.

4. Refresh Sets & Wheels:
- Refresh sets: tpcgen-cli 4.0.0 has NO TPC-H RF1/RF2 or TPC-DS -update options; bundled C dbgen/dsdgen must remain for refresh paths.
- PyPI wheels (Apache-2.0, 13 wheels): macOS arm64/x86_64, manylinux+musllinux (x86_64/aarch64/armv7l/i686/ppc64le), win32/win_amd64; NO win_arm64 wheel. Disposition: keep C binaries for win_arm64 until Phase 3 retirement decision.

Zero repository files or _binaries/ modified.

description:
## Problem
Upstream datafusion-contrib/tpcgen-rs publishes tpcgen-cli 4.0.0 wheels on PyPI covering TPC-H and TPC-DS, and a quick SF 0.01 TPC-H probe matched bundled dbgen after stripping trailing pipes. Before building an adapter, TPC-DS parity, fractional sub-scale behavior, Parquet logical/physical differences, refresh-set coverage, and chunk/stdout framing must be verified empirically.

## Change
- Pin tpcgen-cli 4.0.0 in an isolated scratch environment and execute Gate B checks at SF 0.01, 0.1, and 1.0 for both tpch and tpcds (--compat c):
  1. Delimited SHA-256 byte identity against bundled dbgen/dsdgen after trailing-pipe removal (comparing against normalize_tbl_trailing_delimiters behavior), at --num-threads 1 and default thread count.
  2. TPC-DS fractional sub-scale row counts vs tpcds_subscale_row_counts.json, NULL vs empty-string counts per column, and Latin-1/UTF-8 encoding parity.
  3. Parquet comparison vs BaseFormatConverter: bidirectional DuckDB EXCEPT ALL (must be 0 rows), logical Arrow/Parquet schema comparison, physical layout comparison (row-group size, encodings, statistics), and Parquet-scan query timing delta on DuckDB and DataFusion.
  4. Chunk file naming compatibility with loaders and derived benchmarks (tpchavoc, read_primitives, write_primitives, transaction_primitives, datavault, tpcds_obt), plus stdout/streaming capability for single-pass stripping + compression.
  5. Refresh-set capability check (TPC-H RF1/RF2 and TPC-DS -update) and PyPI wheel platform inventory (confirming Windows arm64 absence).
- Measure wall time (mono_time()) and peak RSS vs legacy generation + conversion.

## Decision gates
- Go/no-go evidence for adopting tpcgen-cli on tpch and tpcds in Phase 1, naming exact adapter shims required.
- If tpcgen-cli fails byte parity on any table or sub-scale, record the exact failing table/column/row and block Phase 1 cutover for that benchmark until resolved upstream or shimmed.
- Confirms which refresh paths still require bundled C dbgen/dsdgen.

## Guardrails
- Run SF 1 checks under make heavy-run ([HEAVY-LOCK-001]) in isolated temp directories deleted after the spike ([RUN-DATA-001]).
- Use SHA-256 byte hashes and EXCEPT ALL (never plain EXCEPT, which ignores duplicate counts); treat 6-sigfig value digests (result_digest.py) as secondary only.
- Never modify shared datagen/ folders or benchbox/_binaries/.
